svg.text: Three ways to encode an instruction: RISC-V, MIPS, x86-64
Fixed 32-bit words with fields in the same places (RISC-V, MIPS) against a variable-length sequence of optional bytes (x86-64). Examples encoded by model/asm.js and model/isas/.
RISC-V: six formats, all 32 bits. rd, rs1 and rs2 are in the same place in every format that has them.
MIPS: three formats, all 32 bits. The opcode is on the left; 16-bit immediates; 26-bit jump targets.
x86-64: one instruction is 1 to 15 bytes, built from optional parts in a fixed order.
The same operations, encoded (bytes as they lie in memory, lowest address first)
RISC-V and MIPS need two instructions (8 bytes) to add a value from memory; x86-64 does it in one 5-byte instruction, which its decoder splits into a load and an add.
